line.line: Come along, no more stops, we need to find our way to Solitude.
Why are we even going to a wedding at this far flung end of the Empire anyway?
Ugh. Speak to my husband, if you must.
I told you, it's the wedding of Vittoria Vici, an extremely well connected merchant with the East Empire Company. The Emperor's cousin? Remember?
Indeed. If we ever get there.
Hopefully these gifts will put us in her good graces, secure that import deal, and lead the way to an audience with the Emperor.
Don't bother me, peasant. I've had a long journey and paid too much coin on these gifts to be late to Vittoria's wedding.
I'm on my way to Solitude to join the Legion. A united Empire is better for everyone.
Loyal Nords are always welcome here. Anyone else better watch their step.
You hear that? I swear there's something out there... in the dark.
Welcome to the Vilemyr Inn. If there's anything I can get you, just let me know.
Skyrim certainly has its fair share of inns.
If you're headed up to the monastery, watch your step... it's a long way down.
I'll show you to your room. Right this way.
This place almost reminds me of my homeland. Almost.
I heard the Gourmet is hiding out somewhere in Skyrim. You know, fella who wrote that cookbook.
Do not give your trust blindly, stranger, it will come back to bite you.
The road takes you many places, but sometimes it's best to pave your own.
Let me know if there's anything else you need.
Just get out of my way, I've got work to do.
Lynly, would you mind taking care of the customer please?
Then I guess that's your last request, fool!
Fool, I will see you dead!
You won't get the best of me!
Are you truly ready to die? I'll try and make this quick!
I will claw the eyes out of you, fool!
You ready to die today? Huh?
You - over here, quick. Before any of them show up!
Please, stranger! I need your help!
If you run into my husband Nazeem, remind him that he's not married to himself.
Mallus is teaching me everything he knows about brewing. Hopefully, I can take over his position some day.
By Ysmir, it's true. A jester - funny suit and all. Just north, by the Loreius Farm. Fool had a coffin in a cart, with a broken wheel.
Like to see him laugh his way out of that.
Just fists. No weapons, no magic... no crying. Let's go!
Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!
Well, well. Another maggot to squash beneath my boot.
Come on. Let's see what you're made of.
Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!
Who taught you to fight? Keep those hands up!
Come on! Keep your guard up and wait for an opening!
Twelve septims on the big one!
Drive that snowback to the ground. Come on!
Come on! Let's see you put up a fight!
That the best you can do?
You think I'm afraid of you?
You're no liar. Best fight I've had in years. There you are.
We'll pay whatever it takes, but we must have more swords for the Imperial soldiers.
I just can't fill an order that size on my own.
Ha! I'd sooner bend my knee to Ulfric Stormcloak.
Have it your way. I'll take the job, but don't expect a miracle.
That's a decent weapon you've made there.
The name's Hjoromir, and I'm just the man for the job.
You sure look like you could use some help.
You sure look like you could use some help.
You sure look like you could use some help.
Anything else I can do for you sir?
You want to keep helping? How about you make some armor. Make sure you have the right raw materials.
Make some armor, got it.  Just need to um...yeah... what do you mean by raw materials?
(Groan) Start by tanning some leather on the rack. A lot of weapons and armor need leather for straps, fittings, that kind of thing.
Well, one of us has to do something!
What are you doing that for?
I said no! No adventures, no theatrics, no thief-chasing!
Well, what are you going to do then, huh? Let's hear it!
We are done talking about this.
Oh, a customer. Sorry you had to hear that.
What are you doing that for?
You could? I've got some coin coming in from my last shipment. It's yours if you bring my claw back.
Now, if you're going to get those thieves, you should head to Bleak Falls Barrow, northwest of town.
So this is your plan, Lucan?
Yes. So now you don't have to go, do you?
Oh really? Well I think your new helper here needs a guide.
Wh- no... I... Oh, by the Eight, fine. But only to the edge of town!
We have to go through town and across the bridge to get to Bleak Falls Barrow.
Wait, so... a costume? You're not serious...
Those thieves must be mad, hiding out there. Those old crypts are filled with nothing but traps, trolls, and who knows what else!
Sure I am. We got some furs and tree branches; paint them white and then tie them to Stump. Instant Frostbite Spider!
Frodnar... nobody is going to believe that your dog is a... Frostbite Spider. And if they do... they'll kill him. That's not much of a prank.
Oh yeah, and what would you rather do?
How about... we play tag! You're it!
Hey, no fair! Get her, Stump!
I wonder why they only stole Lucan's golden claw. I mean, we have plenty of things in the shop that are worth just as much coin.
This is the bridge out of town. The path up the mountain to the northwest leads to Bleak Falls Barrow.
Good luck. Lucan and I will be waiting for you back in the shop.
You're new around here, so I'll go easy on ya. But don't get on my bad side.
The ale is going bad. We need to get a new batch.
That letter ought to convince Camilla to never speak to Faendal ever again.
Come on in. Just stoked the fire. Take a seat and get the cold out.
You're that visitor, been pokin' around.
Let me guess - someone stole your sweetroll...
You're new around here, so I'll go easy on ya. But don't get on my bad side.
Welcome. Let me know if you want anything... think I got a clean mug around here somewhere.
This is a local favorite and one of the first songs I ever learned. Ragnar the Red.
Oh! There once was a hero named Ragnar the Red, who came riding to Whiterun from ole Rorikstead!
And the braggart did swagger and brandish his blade, as he told of bold battles and gold he had made!
But then he went quiet, did Ragnar the Red, when he met the shieldmaiden Matilda who said...
"Oh, you talk and you lie and you drink all our mead! Now I think it's high time that you lie down and bleed!"
And so then came the clashing and slashing of steel, as the brave lass Matilda charged in full of zeal!
And the braggart named Ragnar was boastful no moooooree... when his ugly red head rolled around on the floor!
We drink to our youth, to days come and gone. For the age of aggression is just about done.
We'll drive out the Stormcloaks and restore what we own. With our blood and our steel we'll take back our home.
Down with Ulfric the killer of kings. On the day of your death we'll drink and we'll sing.
We're the children of Skyrim, and we fight all our lives. And when Sovngarde beckons, every one of us dies!
But this land is ours and we'll see it wiped clean. Of the scourge that has sullied our hopes and our dreams.

Thank you, thank you. No, please, hold your applause.

I ain't askin' for much, just a few septims.

Spare a coin for a poor old beggar?

Foolish old woman! You know nothing! Nothing of our struggles, our suffering!
Once I've made enough money trading with the Khajiit caravans, I'm going to buy the Bannered Mare from Hulda.
Nothing? And what of my son? Hmm? What of Thorald? Is he nothing? So don't talk to me about suffering!
Tired of bread and stew? Had enough of fish and fowl? Treat yourself and your kin to a choice cut of steak or a tender rack of ribs!
Your son chose his side, and he chose poorly. And now he's gone. Such is the way of war. The sooner you accept his loss, the better.
The finest cuts, fresh from the wilds!
Chops and steaks fit for a Jarl! Come and see my selection of the finest-quality meats!

Do you believe this old hag?
"Holding him?" Why I've got him in my cellar. He's my prisoner.
Chops and steaks fit for a Jarl! Come and see my selection of the finest-quality meats!
Face it, cow! Your stupid son is dead! He died a Stormcloak traitor. And you... you best keep your mouth shut before you suffer the same.

Come on, Father. There's nothing more to be said here.

Aye, love. Love! Even as man, great Talos cherished us. For he saw in us, in each of us, the future of Skyrim! The future of Tamriel!
Someone's been pilfering crops from my farm. If I find out it's one of your kin, I'll see the culprit rot in prison.
I'm surprised you had the wits to notice, Olfrid, what with your nose buried so far up the Emperor's backside.
And there it is, friends! The ugly truth! We are the children of man! Talos is the true god of man! Ascended from flesh, to rule the realm of spirit!
You won't be laughing when the Thalmor come to root out Stormcloak sympathizers.
The very idea is inconceivable to our Elven overlords! Sharing the heavens with us? With man? Ha! They can barely tolerate our presence on earth!
I'll remember that when the Stormcloaks liberate the city. No amount of money will protect you then, Battle-Born.
Today, they take away your faith. But what of tomorrow? What then? Do the elves take your homes? Your businesses? Your children? Your very lives?
And what does the Empire do? Nothing! Nay, worse than nothing! The Imperial machine enforces the will of the Thalmor! Against its own people!
So rise up! Rise up, children of the Empire! Rise up, Stormcloaks! Embrace the word of mighty Talos, he who is both man and Divine!
Trust in me, Whiterun! Trust in Heimskr! For I am the chosen of Talos! I alone have been anointed by the Ninth to spread his holy word!
Talos the mighty! Talos the unerring! Talos the unassailable! To you we give praise!
Are those two at it again?
Strike when the shoulder turns. He's giving you openings!
But I still hear the call of the blood.
We all do. It is our burden to bear. But we can overcome.
You have my brother and I, obviously. But I don't know if the rest will go along quite so easily.
Would you now? Here, let me have a look at you.
Master, you're not truly considering accepting her?
I am nobody's master, Vilkas. And last I checked, we had some empty beds in Jorrvaskr for those with a fire burning in their hearts.
Apologies. But perhaps this isn't the time. I've never even heard of this outsider.
Sometimes the famous come to us. Sometimes men and women come to us to seek their fame. It makes no difference.
That's the spirit. Vilkas, here, will get started on that.
Vilkas, take her out to the yard and see what she can do.
The old man said to have a look at you, so let's do this.
I'll try and make this quick!
Pretty good arm you have there.
Come on now, fight your own battles.
Come on now, fight your own battles.
You might just make it. But for now, you're still a whelp to us, new blood. So you do what we tell you.
This isn't a command. Just decency. Help out an old blacksmith. I've got to get back to my work.
I told you, this is the whelp that Vilkas mentioned.
Ah, yes. I heard you gave him quite the thrashing.
Don't let Vilkas catch you saying that.
Here, let's have Farkas show you where you'll be resting your head.
New blood? Oh, hello. I'm Farkas. Come, follow me.
Skjor and Aela like to tease me, but they're good people.
Nice to have a new face around. It gets boring here sometimes.
The quarters are up here. Just pick a bed and fall in it when you're tired.
All right, so here you are. Looks like the others are eager to meet you.
I was the newest Companion, until you came along. I guess that's okay. Just means I can show you the ropes!
Come to me with questions. I know our history almost as well as Vignar by now. Except I can remember it.
We are but maggots, writhing in the filth of our own corruption! While you have ascended from the dung of mortality, and now walk among the stars!
There is a thing you could do for me. Suitable for someone of your particular talents, perhaps.
I serve Jarl Baalgruuf as steward.
Farengar, I think I've found someone who can help you with your dragon project.
Go ahead and fill her in with all the details.
If I said that was a tedious question, would you be smart enough to know what I meant? Probably not.
This is a priority now. Anything we can use to fight this dragon, or dragons. We need it, quickly. Before it's too late.
Of course, Jarl Balgruuf. You seem to have found me an able assistant.
I'm sure she will prove most useful.
Succeed at this, and you'll be rewarded. Whiterun will be in your debt.

Don't forget to check inside the shop if you need anything.
Do you have news of our quarry?
She cannot hide from us forever.

No more! I yield! I yield!

Singing "Oh willow waly" by the tree that weeps with me. Singing "Oh willow waly" till my lover return to me.

May your shield be stout, and your sword steady.
Come and see me again sometime. I might have some use for you.

I can't believe we let provincials like you wander Skyrim.

We make such a good team!
What are you doing that for?
Come on, is that all you've got?
Pray to your gods for mercy!
I'll have your toes cut off, come on!
I'll show you a real fight!
Sometimes I wonder if using a one-handed weapon would be more suitable for my frame, but it really doesn't suit my personality.
Is this some sort of Orc Stronghold?  These ones are a lot meaner.  Which is saying something.
Can't a man have a bit of privacy? Get out of here!
..."Go to the college," Da said... "Use your smarts," he said... like I'm supposed to figure out which college he meant...
This will be fun. Come on!
Today is a good day to die, heh. For you!
Pray to Stendarr while you can!
Looking for the blade? You aren't the first!
This Orc was very well read. The Real Barenziah? The Life of Uriel Septim? A student of history! Oh and a ruined book too! I'm sure that's a mistake.
And that's the last of them.
If the accident never happened, I would be wed to some dashing noble. But how would you ever manage without me?
That's it. On to the next battle. Or maybe the next inn.
You won't put me in a cage, warlock!
Yes, suppose it's not something you see very often in Skyrim, is it?
Excellent. I'm looking forward to it.
Woah... How are you feeling? You look awful.
I think I learned something from that fight. Don't get hit.
Ah, a snitch, eh? Can't have you running to any guards now, can I?
Give up while you still can!
Argh! You dare challenge a child of Malacath? Die, damn you!
I'll have your head for a trophy!
And that's the last of them.
My lady, are you not tired?  It is well past both our bedtimes.
I think I might've hurt my wrist. No, wait, it was that one's head.
That the best you can do?
That was a very tough fight. I think even my scars have scars.

Oh, I can smell your blood...

I will claw the eyes out of you, fool!

Our hero, our hero, claims a warrior's heart.
I tell you, I tell you, the Dragonborn comes.

It's an end to the evil, of all Skyrim's foes.
For the darkness has passed, and the legend yet grows.
You'll know, You'll know the Dragonborn's come.

Damn leg's playing up... I should see a healer one of these days.
Whatever you need. By Ysmir, if it's simple and strong, I can forge it.
Mara bless you for agreeing to help us.
How do you feel? I think you might be sick.
Papa says I'm too friendly with strangers, but you seem all right.
We don't need to be talking.

And deserve our praise you do, for we are one! Ere you ascended and the Eight became Nine, you walked among us, great Talos, not as god, but as man!

It's the leaving that's hardest, I know.
Talos the mighty! Talos the unerring! Talos the unassailable! To you we give praise!
Are you feeling all right, dear? You look a little ill.
Heard they're reforming the Dawnguard. Vampire hunters or something, in the old fort near Riften. Might consider joining up myself.
And deserve our praise you do, for we are one! Ere you ascended and the Eight became Nine, you walked among us, great Talos, not as god, but as man!
I trust you're not planning any trouble. What can I do for you, friend?
That was fun. Fighting is a good way to lose weight. Except if you lose. Then it's very, very bad.
I've heard there are healers so talented they can heal almost any scar. I'm sure my Thane will find them for me.  No pressure.
You fight as bad as you smell, troll!
We make such a good team!
Ha ha! I love a challenge!
You won't live to see tomorrow!
Whatcha gonna do? Huh? Whatcha gonna do?
Come on! She's not so tough!
